name: Swan Quarter National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Sixteen thousand acres of brackish marsh and cypress swamp on Pamlico Sound, with a boat ramp, a wildlife drive and wintering waterfowl by the thousand.
buzz: Best in winter for ducks and swans, and the drive is easy. Bring bug spray and a scope.

name: Ocracoke Pony Pen
unique: A fenced pasture on Ocracoke where the descendants of the island's wild Banker ponies live, with an observation platform and a short trail.
buzz: The ponies are smaller and shaggier than expected, and the story of how they got here is the fun part. Free and quick.

name: Stone Mountain State Park
unique: A 600 foot granite dome with a loop trail, a waterfall, a historic mountain farm and trout streams, on the Blue Ridge escarpment.
buzz: The summit loop is steep and worth it, with a view that feels much higher than it is. Go early for parking.

name: Wilkes Heritage Museum
unique: A county museum in the 1902 courthouse with a moonshine still, a NASCAR room and the story of the Wilkes County music scene that fed MerleFest.
buzz: The moonshine and racing rooms are the draw, and the old courtroom is worth the visit alone.

name: Childress Vineyards
unique: A NASCAR owner's winery with a Tuscan style tasting room, a bistro and vines rolling over the Piedmont, just off the interstate.
buzz: The setting is the sell and the tastings are organized. Book the bistro for lunch on a weekend.

name: Uptown Lexington
unique: A courthouse square ringed by barbecue joints, antique shops and a historic theater, in the town that calls itself the barbecue capital of the world.
buzz: The wood smoked barbecue is the reason, and the square is walkable. Most pits sell out by mid afternoon.

name: Linville Falls
unique: A three tier waterfall on the Linville River dropping into Linville Gorge, with four overlooks reached by short trails from the Blue Ridge Parkway.
buzz: The upper falls are an easy walk and the gorge view is the payoff. Parking fills by mid morning in fall.

name: Linville Caverns
unique: A guided walk through a limestone cave under Humpback Mountain, with stalactites, a subterranean stream and trout that live in the dark.
buzz: The tour is short and cool, a good hot day activity. It is commercial, but the cave is real.

name: Wheels Through Time Museum
unique: A museum of rare American motorcycles, with boards of speed records, dirt track racers and military bikes, most of them in running condition.
buzz: The curator starts engines, which makes it more alive than a normal museum. Even non riders enjoy it.

name: Waynesville Main Street
unique: A mountain main street of brick storefronts, a courthouse, galleries and a brewery, with the Frog Level arts district downhill.
buzz: The street is walkable and busy on weekends, with good coffee and a Friday night music scene.

name: Chatuge Lake
unique: A TVA reservoir on the Hiwassee with wooded coves, a swimming beach and a view of the mountains on both sides, at the far western tip of the state.
buzz: Warm water and quiet coves, good for swimming and bass. Rentals are limited, so bring a boat or a kayak.

name: Clay County Courthouse
unique: A small courthouse on a square in the smallest county seat in the state, surrounded by mountains and a few storefronts.
buzz: A two minute stop, but the square and the setting are pretty. Pair it with the lake.

name: Fontana Lake
unique: A deep lake backed up behind the tallest dam east of the Rockies, with the Great Smoky Mountains on one side and the Nantahala forest on the other.
buzz: The drive along the lake is the attraction, with pullouts and swimming holes. The dam tour is seasonal.

name: Joyce Kilmer Memorial Forest
unique: A 3,800 acre old growth forest with tulip poplars over 20 feet around, preserved as a memorial to the poet, reached by a two mile loop trail.
buzz: The trees are genuinely enormous and the trail is easy. Go in spring for wildflowers and autumn for color.

name: Kings Mountain Gateway Trail
unique: A paved trail through town that climbs toward the national military park, connecting the depot, the parks and eventually the battlefield.
buzz: A good local greenway with a climb at the end. The battlefield is the destination.

name: Shelby Courthouse Square
unique: A 1907 courthouse on a square with a fountain, storefronts and a statue of Earl Scruggs, in the banjo player's home county.
buzz: The square is small and walkable, and the Earl Scruggs Center is a block away.

name: Alamance Battleground
unique: The field where Regulator farmers fought the colonial militia in 1771, a prelude to the Revolution, with a visitor center and a walking trail.
buzz: The story is lesser known and well told, and the site is quiet. Free and worth an hour.

name: Burlington City Park
unique: A 75 acre park with a 1911 carousel, a miniature train, a lake and a stadium, in the middle of a textile town.
buzz: The carousel and train are a dollar or two and still run. A good cheap afternoon with small kids.

name: French Broad River Rafting
unique: Class II and III whitewater on one of the oldest rivers in the world, with a hot spring town at the takeout and the Appalachian Trail crossing the bridge.
buzz: Big enough for a thrill and safe enough for beginners. The hot tubs in town are the recovery plan.

name: Mars Hill University
unique: A small mountain college campus with brick buildings, a quad and a view of the Black Mountains, founded before the Civil War.
buzz: Quiet and pretty, with a good coffee shop in town. The view from the upper campus is the reward.

name: Rockingham Speedway
unique: The one mile oval known as The Rock, a former NASCAR track with steep banks and a gritty history, now hosting regional and club races.
buzz: The track is legendary and the events are low key. Check the schedule, because it is not a weekly show.

name: Richmond County Museum
unique: A county museum with railroad and textile history, Native American artifacts and the story of the Rockingham speedway era.
buzz: Volunteer run and free, with racing memorabilia in the corner. Call first.

name: Bynum Bridge
unique: A 1922 cotton mill bridge turned pedestrian crossing over the Haw River, with graffiti, rope swings and a swimming hole below.
buzz: The bridge is a local hangout with a view of the river and the old mill ruins. Park at the Bynum lot.

name: Fearrington Village
unique: A planned village with gardens, shops, a bookstore and Belted Galloway cows grazing beside the lawn, built around a 19th century farm.
buzz: The cows are the photo and the bookstore and cafe make it a stop. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Historic Halifax
unique: A preserved colonial river town where North Carolina's 1776 independence resolutions were adopted, with the courthouse, tavern and houses still standing.
buzz: The site is quiet and the story is foundational. Start at the visitor center and walk the street.

name: Roanoke Rapids Lake
unique: A reservoir on the Roanoke with public ramps, fishing piers and a beach at the dam, good for bass and catfish.
buzz: The lake is quiet and the fishing is the point. Check access points before towing a boat.

name: Roan Mountain Gardens
unique: A high grassy bald on the Appalachian Trail with the largest natural rhododendron garden in the world, blooming purple in mid June.
buzz: The June bloom is a genuine spectacle and the balds feel like another state. Bring a jacket.

name: Emerald Village
unique: A former feldspar and mica mine where you can pan for gems, tour the underground workings and see the equipment that supplied the region's mineral industry.
buzz: The gem panning is the kid hit and the mine tour is genuinely underground. Allow two hours.
